name: RDKit
subcategory: open-source cheminformatics and molecular machine-learning toolkit
origin_detail: Developed by Greg Landrum with contributions from the RDKit open-source community; first released in 2006 (SourceForge project registered 16 Feb 2006, described as 'cheminformatics and machine-learning software written in C++ and Python'). Commercial support is provided by T5 Informatics GmbH. The commonly told pre-2006 history (development at Rational Discovery LLC, later Novartis support) was not confirmed in the fetched sources.
openness_notes: BSD-3-Clause ('business-friendly BSD license') since release. Stewarded by its lead developer and community without a foundation, so scored 3; commercial support comes from T5 Informatics rather than an open-core product.
risk_events: Key-person concentration: copyright line reads 'Greg Landrum and other RDKit contributors' and the project depends heavily on its lead developer; no foundation or named funder was found on the fetched pages.
robustness: Active quarterly release cadence (2026.09.1 on 3 Oct and 2026.09.2 on 5 Nov 2026), 8,788 commits, 3.7k GitHub stars and 1.1k forks; permissive licence means anyone can fork. Very heavy downstream use (~6.9 million PyPI downloads a month) makes it critical infrastructure with thin formal support.
physical_science_relevance: The default open cheminformatics toolkit for molecular featurisation, SMILES/graph handling and descriptor generation in chemistry and drug-discovery machine learning; widely embedded in AI pipelines for molecules.
openness_effect_assessment: A permissive licence let RDKit become the standard molecular toolkit in open and commercial ML pipelines, reflected in millions of monthly downloads. The cost is that a very widely used dependency rests on a small core team and a services company, with no visible institutional funding.
key_takeaway: RDKit is the open-source chemistry analogue of the scientific Python stack: free, permissive, and woven into nearly every molecular-ML workflow, with usage (millions of downloads per month) far outrunning its visible funding. It is a prime example of AI-era value accruing on top of thinly resourced open infrastructure.
funding_sources: Commercial support and services via T5 Informatics GmbH
